Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary TUP Depending on the number of players, play with the following cards: 4 players: Take all cards. 3 players: Remove cards numbered 58 to 75 and return them to the box. 2 players: Remove cards numbered 40 to 75 and return them to the box. Place a Scorecard in front of you. Shuffle the cards and place 3 cards face-up in the center of the table. Then deal 18 cards to each player. Place them face-down in a row in front of you, with the dark sea side facing down. Make sure you can insert and remove cards without disturbing the order. Hint: Cards should not overlap or as little as possible to ensure easy handling. fish next to them, but face-down cards, Corals, and Octopuses don’t bother them. Octopus want to hide in the Corals: an Octopus between 2 Corals of any color: 4 points. If adjacent to only 1 Coral: 2 points. If not next to any Corals: 0 points. Corals like variety: check all your Coral cards and count how many complete sets of pink + green + yellow you have, regardless of their position. Each set of 3 different Coral colors: 3 points. Anchor cards (anchor side up): Now, count how many Anchor cards you have. Each Anchor card scores minus points. If you have several, add up all the minus points per card, regardless of their position: 1st card: -1 point | 2nd card: -2 points 3rd card: -3 points | 4th card: -4 points 5th card: -5 points and so on... The player with the highest score wins. In case of a tie, the player with fewest Anchor cards wins. All your face-down cards score 0 and remain in place as separators. You also score Anchor cards. Minus points will be deducted later. Bannerfish want to gather: a group consists of 2 to 4+ adjacent Banner-fish, no other face-up or face-down cards between them: • 1 Bannerfish: 0 points • 2 Bannerfish: 2 points • 3 Bannerfish: 5 points • 4+ Bannerfish: 9 points Pufferfish prefer to be alone: a Puffer-fish with no fish adjacent scores 3 points. Bannerfish love sticking closely to their buddies. Pufferfish prefer their space. Keep bannerfish together and pufferfish apart! Octopus and coral also play an important role in your biome, so place them wisely to score more points. Score by building the best hand. But here’s the twist: everyone starts with face-down cards and must slot new cards into their hand in ascending order, revealing their strategy one card at a time.

1. Start with your cards face-down. Draw a card from the center.
2. Place it face-up in ascending order. Then reveal the adjacent card.
3. Keep your sea dwellers happy to win, but avoid penalties.

Who will dive the smartest and reel in the most points?

—description from the publisher
community_text:
[Rating: 3/10] After 1 solo game on BGA: Thematically, it dives deep into the ocean, but in terms of gameplay depth, it barely goes below sea level. You have very little agency. Which card you draw is based on luck, and then you estimate the appropriate slot for that card considering the species, the number printed on it, and what other players have already played. This feels bland. By the end, things inevitably get tight and awkward, and you have to take some losses. This feels bad. [Rating: 5/10] You get to a point in a game where you're better off just not trying to improve your tableau anymore and I didn't like that at all.

[Rating: 6/10] Tried on BGA. Feels a lot like the recent Ipso, to the point where I double-checked that it wasn't by the same designer. Except instead of building multiple lines in that one you're just doing one line, and there's a very light theme to this to add more specific scoring.  Just like in Ipso, there's not much agency. Just wait until your turn, pick one of the available cards, and put it somewhere in your line that you think works best. I've bumped this up a bit more than Ipso just because it at least included attractive art, and has the hint of a theme to it (but barely).  Also not much exciteme

[Rating: 6/10] Jeu découvert sur BGA, j'ai eu l'occasion d'y jouer avec l'auteur Flavio Foches. J'ai actuellement 4/5 parties, les parties s'enchainent assez vite, comptez environ 15 mn la partie. les règles ne sont pas complexes et rapides à s'approprier mais avec une certes profondeurs. C'est selon moi un jeu familial, type apéro pour démarrer une session jeux de cartes.

[Rating: 6/10] Played on BGA. Solo.  Quick Nice artwork  Bit like “welcome to” but with Octopus and Pufferfish.
